entry.title: Harriet Farlow - 2026 UNSW Young Alumni Award Winner

media:group.media:title: Harriet Farlow - 2026 UNSW Young Alumni Award Winner
media:group.media:description:
"If my story inspires others in any way, it's that I hope that everyone embraces their unique gifts and abilities and fearlessly uses them to create some kind of positive impact in the world"
Meet the winner of the 2026 UNSW Young Alumni Award, Harriet Farlow.
Dr Harriet Farlow is an AI security researcher, entrepreneur, author and educator with more than a decade of experience across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, government, academia and industry. She is Founder and CEO of Mileva Security Labs, Australia’s first AI security company, helping organisations manage emerging AI risks through training, advisory services and technical education.
Previously, Harriet served as Acting Technical Director of the AI Hub at the Australian Signals Directorate. She holds a PhD from UNSW Canberra and authored Practical AI Security. Harriet speaks internationally, leads the HarrietHacks YouTube channel and serves on the board of Good Ancestors.

entry.title: Adele Schonhardt OAM - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Art & Culture

media:group.media:title: Adele Schonhardt OAM - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Art & Culture
media:group.media:description:
"When you think about what you did during the pandemic, during those dark years where you were stuck at home, you turned to music."
Meet the winner of the 2026 UNSW Alumni Award for Art & Culture, Adele Schonhardt OAM.
Adele Schonhardt OAM is an arts executive with experience across Australia, Germany and the United States. A Melbourne Conservatorium of Music graduate, she holds an Executive MBA from AGSM, UNSW. Adele is Executive Director of Melbourne Chamber Orchestra, following leadership roles with Musica Viva Australia, Germany’s classical music sector and the League of American Orchestras in New York.
In 2020, she co-founded the Australian Digital Concert Hall, which streamed more than 1,000 performances and generated over $4 million for artists and arts organisations. A recipient of multiple awards, Adele was awarded the OAM for service to the arts in 2024.

entry.title: Ben Farinazzo - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Community Service

media:group.media:title: Ben Farinazzo - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Community Service
media:group.media:description:
"Service gave me identity. Recovery taught me a deeper form of strength. Invictus, it gave me hope. Community gave that hope somewhere to go."
Meet the winner of the 2026 UNSW Alumni Award for Community Service, Ben Farinazzo.
Ben Farinazzo is a proud Australian with Italian and Aboriginal heritage. He is a former Australian Army officer and CEO, two-time Invictus Games gold medalist, Australia Day Ambassador and mental health advocate.
Ben served on active deployment in East Timor and built a senior leadership career in Australia and overseas. After recovering from severe PTSD, anxiety, depression and serious spinal injuries, Ben represented Australia at the 2018 Invictus Games Sydney, winning two gold medals.
Today, he supports veteran and community wellbeing and is developing a 1,000km national pilgrimage connecting people, landscapes, communities and Country across Australia.

entry.title: Vincent Allen - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Innovation & Entrepreneurship

media:group.media:title: Vincent Allen - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Innovation & Entrepreneurship
media:group.media:description:
"We are the first generation to feel the impacts of climate change, but we may also be the last generation to do something about it."
Meet the winner of the 2026 UNSW Alumni Award for Innovation & Entrepreneurship, Vincent Allen.
Vincent Allen is the co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of SunDrive, a solar technology company launched while completing his PhD at UNSW. He helped develop breakthrough copper-based solar cells and has led their progression from university research to pilot-scale manufacturing.
SunDrive replaces silver in solar panels with abundant, lower-cost copper, enabling more scalable production. Under Vince’s leadership, the company set a world record for commercial-size silicon solar-cell efficiency in 2021 and built the world’s first fully automated direct-copper-plating HJT pilot line in 2024.

entry.title: Doug Crawford - 2026 UNSW Alumni Awards Winner of The Chancellor's Award in Memoriam

media:group.media:title: Doug Crawford - 2026 UNSW Alumni Awards Winner of The Chancellor's Award in Memoriam
media:group.media:description:
"It's important that we learn to win gracefully, and lose gracefully, and that's what helps our civilisation develop".
This year, Doug Crawford has been awarded The Chancellor's Award in Memoriam in the UNSW Alumni Awards.
Doug Crawford (1933–2025) was a pioneering leader and servant of UNSW Sport. His connection with UNSW began in 1951 as an engineering student, founding member of the Boat and Rifle Clubs, and talented sprinter. After injury ended his Olympic aspirations, he became athletics team manager at the 1956 Melbourne intervarsity.
From 1954 to 1967, Doug served as secretary, treasurer and president of the UNSW Sports Association, remaining its longest-serving president. He helped establish the Injury Assistance Scheme, championed the Link Building and created the Ben Lexcen Scholarship.
A mentor and leader, Doug’s legacy continues through generations of student athletes.

entry.title: Professor Elizabeth Taylor AO - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Research & Education Excellence

media:group.media:title: Professor Elizabeth Taylor AO - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Research & Education Excellence
media:group.media:description:
"The strength of having diversity in any situation is that the solutions are far more robust, far more appropriate to the situation rather than a singular view of the world"
Meet the winner of the 2026 UNSW Alumni Award for Research & Education Excellence, Professor Elizabeth Taylor AO.
Elizabeth Taylor AO is an engineer, governance specialist and Emeritus Professor at Central Queensland University, with a career spanning industry, design and construction, academia and leadership. She is Chair of SmartCrete CRC and the International Engineering Alliance’s Governing Group and Sydney Accord, and a former Chair of the Washington Accord and Engineers Australia Accreditation Board.
Elizabeth contributes to humanitarian and community causes, currently chairing the Cambodian Children’s Trust Australia. An Honorary Fellow of Engineers Australia and Fellow of ATSE and AICD, she has been recognised among Australia’s 100 influential engineers and received Engineers Australia’s 2021 Peter Nicol Russell Career Achievement Memorial Medal.

entry.title: Professor Jane Catherine Ngila - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Professional Achievement

media:group.media:title: Professor Jane Catherine Ngila - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Professional Achievement
media:group.media:description:
"It was a rough life. I grew up feeling that I just needed to get out of this situation, and I said education is going to be my tool, my ticket, my instrument, my vehicle, to get out of this situation."
Meet the winner of the 2026 UNSW Alumni Award for Professional Achievement, Professor Jane Catherine Ngila.
Professor Jane Catherine Ngila is the Executive Director of the African Foundation for Women and Youth in Education, Science, Technology and Innovation (AFoWYESTI), advancing quality education and mentorship for women and youth in STEM.
Prof. Ngila has taught at many universities including the University of Johannesburg and the University of Botswana, in various courses in analytical and environmental chemistry. She is also a Member of the UNESCO Global Multistakeholder Advisory Committee for Women and Girls in Science, a Council Member for the United Nations University and holds other senior leadership and strategic roles.
Her award-winning research in analytical and environmental chemistry focuses on water quality, nanotechnology and wastewater treatment.

entry.title: ThinkMD - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Social Impact

media:group.media:title: ThinkMD - 2026 UNSW Alumni Award Winner for Social Impact
media:group.media:description:
"ThinkMD is trying to solve one of the most urgent, meaningful and complex problems on earth, which is how to scale healthcare in regions of the world without access to doctors".
Meet the winners of the 2026 UNSW Alumni Award for Social Impact, the team behind ThinkMD, Christopher Marr DSM, Rodney Davis and Dr Jacqueline Rabec.
ThinkMD is a pioneering MedTech company working to create a world where everyone can access quality healthcare, regardless of where they live. Its innovative clinical decision-support platform empowers frontline healthcare workers with the knowledge and tools to assess patients, support diagnoses and provide appropriate treatment—even in remote communities where doctors are scarce.
Designed to work online and offline, ThinkMD is helping strengthen local health systems and address global health inequalities. By combining clinical expertise, technology and machine learning, ThinkMD is transforming the way care is delivered and bringing hope, dignity and better health outcomes to communities around the world.

media:group.media:title: Regenerating The Heart Using Silk
media:group.media:description:
Professor Jelena Rnjak-Kovacina leads a research group using silk-based biomaterials for cardiovascular repair.
“I have always had an interest in working on natural materials for regenerative medicine and tissue engineering,” Prof. Rnjak-Kovacina says. Her focus extends from the simple fact that the human body is largely built from proteins. And natural materials, also based on proteins, can help reduce unwanted reactions and improve integration.
“Our bodies tend to react better to natural materials than synthetic materials,” Prof. Rnjak-Kovacina says.
As silk is one of nature's strongest fibres, she says it is uniquely processable into materials with tailorable shapes, morphologies and mechanical properties, “allowing us to mimic the features of a native tissue matrix’.”
The main premise of Prof. Rnjak-Kovacina’s work is for the implant to be replaced with native tissue over time – instead of replacing function with permanent implants – building temporary structures where cells migrate, remodel and the patient’s own living tissue takes over as the silk slowly dissolves.
“It’s truly that regenerative medicine approach,” she says.
